rows.title: Hammerspoon SIGTRAPs sending to an hs CLI client whose port is dying
rows.note: Four crashes, one cause: Hammerspoon sends synchronously to an hs client that is gone or going, and CFMessagePortSendRequest SIGTRAPs (PAC check on the freed port). 10-02, 10-03, 10-08: the COMMAND's RETURN to a client that gave up queued behind another suite (first fix: every test hs call under /usr/bin/lockf /tmp/hs-cli.lock with hs -t >= 20, tests/test_hs_cli_lock.sh in both repos). 10-14 03:40: init.lua's print shim, under an hs.task callback, cloned a background print to every non-quiet client, here one exiting (second fix: hammerspoon/ipc_print.lua clones only to the client whose command runs, or to hs -C). Still open, same chain: production callers run hs unlocked with the default 4 s -t (llm-legs bin/claude-chat-switch, claude-resume-timer, llm-selfcheck, llm-reset-redeem; hammerspoon bin/claude-keys, claude-latency; claude-setup hooks/compact-auto.sh, session-trash.sh; the BTT TypeWhisper.toggle action) and can outlive -t behind a long command. Ruled out: AX polling and leaked drawings (in no faulting stack). 10-30 (system-system-20261030T023135Z-005c): the 10-29 20:03:20 crash is a new shape: SIGSEGV in lua_pushboolean right after ipc_sendMessage inside ipc_callback (a CLI command's Lua), the lua_State pointer overwritten by string bytes, 3.7 s after an in-process config reload (notify.log 20:03:17 initial signals; relaunch 20:03:23); no landing touched a watched .lua then. Which client and command ran is blind_spots hs-client-of-crash; not fixable from here.

rows.title: bash segfaults popping limit_hit_bytes' local LC_ALL in a subshell
rows.note: Five bash crash reports (10-29 07:26, 10-30 01:24-01:34), one stack: execute_function -> pop_var_context -> sv_locale -> libintl_setlocale -> CFLocaleCopyPreferredLanguages -> CFPrefs, SIGSEGV on the child side of a fork (CoreFoundation: single-threaded process forked). The function was share/limit-hit.sh limit_hit_bytes (local LC_ALL=C), reached from timeout_command's limit_hit inside $(...): the four 10-30 crashes fall on the four `check-failed` lines of update.log (npm view timed out under load), and no probe.cli hit was journaled for them. The same stack crashed com.llm-refresh three times on 10-28 (llm-refresh and llm-limits.sh source limit-hit.sh). Fix: limit_hit_bytes keeps ${#1} for ASCII text and counts any other text with wc -c, no locale switch. Same class swept (no crash report yet): the four other local LC_* sites in share/ and bin/ are gone (byte counts via limit_hit_bytes, instruction_sub_bytes via LC_ALL=C tr, wait_print_rows perl without a UTF-8 caller, worker-run-backstop's run_dirs sorted by sort), and test_consistency row ep fails on any new one.

rows.title: com.egor.harness-doctor exits 1 while the Speed collector it execs ends in KeyError on a Lost time class with no lever
rows.note: The 7 exit-1 runs (harvest 10-09 18:26..10-10 00:26) are bin/speed-doctor, which harness-doctor's exec_speed replaces itself with, so its exit is the job's: ~/Library/Logs/harness-doctor.log ends in 7 'Speed: error · KeyError: 'refusal'' lines (log mtime 22:42), a 5-min job between share/time_budget.py gaining the refusal class and 9d76b38b (22:47) adding its TIME_LEVERS entry; the next harvest (16 runs) has none. Fix here: tests/test_speed_doctor.sh pins every time_budget.LABEL class and gate refusal row to a TIME_LEVERS lever (red with the refusal lever removed). Ruled out: harness-doctor's own collect (guarded_collect turns its exceptions into an error document; the log's older TypeError tracebacks predate the window, their line numbers match a <3,000-line file vs 6,268 now); exit 1 on a Speed error stays, the menu shows it too.

rows.title: Hammerspoon's own CPU: the 100 ms Terminal tab poll
rows.note: B 7.1 by C, 6,127 cpu-s a day: the AX walk of claude_cmd_keys' 100 ms Terminal tab poll (own CPU 130-510 s an hour on 10-13/14, its reaped osascript/ps 1-7 s). rows.title: statusline.sh render CPU
rows.note: B 3.2 by C, 2,740 cpu-s a day over ~150k renders a day of real chats (3 s refresh stays, Egor's decision), ~109 ms CPU each on 10-13. Cuts: the away replay (llm-legs@3332845a, 10-14 02:55, ~21 ms a replay; 10-14 averaged 64 ms a render) and repo_dirs/input-parse forks (3 fewer processes a worktree render, ~2.5 ms). Left, measured on a warm sandbox render (~65 ms): git status 13 ms, git rev-parse 7 ms, each jq 4-5 ms (input parse, wall view, rate-limit bucket, store stale), the rest bash itself; a rev-parse or wall-view memo needs the statusline contract's event list and tests. 10-29 (system-system-20261029T112240Z-5eba): blind_spots cohort-proof-statusline still holds (llm-legs@7d0d54fb cut the second untracked walk the same day); nothing measurable here. 10-30 (system-system-20261030T023135Z-005c): proof refused again, cores 0.0 before and after (renders are claude's reaped CPU, not tick CPU); blind_spots cohort-proof-statusline holds.

rows.title: review-anchors rewrote its whole blob memo for every hashed chunk
rows.note: B 1.1 by D, 1.2 GB written a day, bursts to 1.6 GB an hour. review-bench and review-debt load review-anchors in-process; stored_blobs rewrote ~/.cache/review-bench/blob-memo/<repo>.json after every 1000-path chunk, and logo-vectorizer-bench's is 74,272 paths (12 MB) with ~100 stale per run: 12 MB per pricing to bank ~16 KB (ssd-sampler: 12 MB into that dir per 2-minute sample). rows.title: memlogd tick CPU
rows.note: B 1.9 by C, all reaped (own CPU 40-96 s a day): every 15 s tick ran chat-load sample (~185 ms CPU, python) and ps -axo rss=,comm= (~43 ms). Half of chat-load was registered_roots: glob of ~2,400 run folders' meta.json plus a listing of ~540 bench folders (~35k files). Cut: ended runs skipped on exit_code before meta.json, bench folders relisted only when their mtime moves (chat-load.benches.json, written only on change); same roots on a fixture (run-name sort, hidden names, dangling meta, pid files added and removed), 186 -> 145 ms CPU a sample. Left: chat-load's ps (~45 ms) and memlogd's node_stats ps (~43 ms) read the same table twice a tick; merging them moves the node counts into chat-load's output, a memory-guard interface change. 10-29 (system-system-20261029T053432Z-424a), by its launchd coalition: 45 tasks and ~0.3 cpu-s a quiet tick; each ps -axo costs ~110 ms CPU on ~900 processes (-c saves only 25 ms), python start ~90 ms, chat-load's own work ~90 ms, the bash forks ~30 ms. The proof's rise since 10-28 22:02 is that day's orphans() (llm-legs@1278e2a0): a launchctl list (~10 ms) and tree_of per candidate each tick while any orphan exists. Next lever: one ps a tick (memlogd runs the full-field ps, takes node stats from it and pipes the text to chat-load sample), then a persistent sampler instead of a python start per tick; tests/test_memlogd.sh's fake ps serves the two field lists separately and needs merging with it. 10-29 (system-system-20261029T112240Z-5eba): the proof's 0.007 -> 0.011 cores coincides with incident ticks at 1 Hz (82 on 10-27, 1,825 on 10-29) and the proof does not divide by ticks; blind_spots cohort-proof-work-mix. 10-30 (system-system-20261030T023135Z-005c): 0.007 -> 0.014 cores coincides with the incident ticks (job-cost:com.egor.memlogd); blind_spots cohort-proof-work-mix still holds.

rows.title: image-fanout scheduler forks
rows.note: B 4.3 by C, on media days (10-15 10.8k, 10-16 12.4k cpu-s). Cut: now_ms sets clock_ms, pick_account sets picked, account_index sets account_at; stub run of 8 takes on one account: same plan table (md5) and files, 2.0 -> 1.5 cpu-s. rows.title: run-suites reaped suite CPU
rows.note: Ruled out as run-suites' own cost (system-system-20261020T113826Z-7b45): its own CPU is ~0 since 10-15 (builtin sleep, kill -0 watchers); its C is the suites' CPU it reaps, below the run journal's own suite cpu_s every day (10-14 37.8k of 83.0k, 10-19 16.9k of 25.7k, 10-20 5.2k of 10.5k). rows.title: worker-run watchdog transcript re-parse
rows.note: Undecided, run system-system-20261020T113826Z-7b45 stopped by Egor mid-problem. C is steady watchdog cost outside suite ticks (10-18 1.9k, 10-19 1.9k cpu-s; 1-20 s a tick over 674 ticks). Each hop (<= 30 s) on a moved transcript runs activity_fingerprint -> compute_transcript_files: transcript_files' two full jq passes (78 ms on a 2.4 MB transcript), transcript_wrote_through_shell's jq pass plus a python3 classifier, though the watchdog reads only RUN_FILES_LIST; estimated ~4.6k cpu-s a day over 154 claudeb runs (76 h) in 2 days. Ready levers: skip transcript_wrote_through_shell in the watchdog (its outputs are unread there); one jq (reduce inputs into bad ids and [id, path] hits, non-string ids tojson) gives byte-identical lists on 138 real transcripts with subagents and a since cut; next, parse only bytes appended since the last hop. Fixed 2026-10-20: levers 1 and 2 applied. The watchdog hop (activity_fingerprint) and last_edit_age call compute_transcript_files <dir> list, which skips transcript_wrote_through_shell (no jq pass, no python3 start); transcript_files reads failed ids and hits in one jq reduce. Proof: byte-identical lists, old vs new, on 165 real transcripts (the 30 largest up to 195 MB, 20 with subagents, a since cut); dropping the failed-id filter diverges on 4, so the filter is exercised; transcript_files 284 -> 151 s over the set, and the shell pass (about half a hop on a typical 2 MB transcript) is gone from the hop. Lever 3 (append-only parse) not taken: one jq start per moved hop remains, reopen with it if the check does not settle. 10-29 (system-system-20261029T053432Z-424a): the proof restarted at llm-legs@e5d5a655 (10-28 23:18, the split into 15 sourced share/worker-run-*.sh modules, the same code parsed per start), so its 8.6 h after-window is only the night's worker load against a 7-day day-and-night baseline (births 6.6 -> 10.6/s with it); undecided until a window holding days, then lever 3. 10-29 (system-system-20261029T112240Z-5eba): 14.0 h after against 3.2 h needed, still a night-heavy after-window against a day-and-night baseline, CPU 0.026 -> 0.058 cores; the proof does not divide by worker runs; blind_spots cohort-proof-work-mix.

fixes.by: Workers и review bench унификация отображения

rows.title: log-sweep walks every kept unit whole
rows.note: 10-29 04:00 the daily sweep hit system-doctor's 1800 s timeout (33 cpu-s): wall is throttled disk I/O (low_priority, IOPOL_THROTTLE) under the night's disk load, sweep 10-15 s until 10-20, 100-650 s since 10-21. Its walk stat()s all ~547k files of the swept stores (pnpm-store 186k, tmp-sandboxes 118k, work-tmp 90k, library and chromium caches 65k each) though a days-criterion unit only needs one mtime newer than its keep. Cut: measure(entry, settled) stops a unit's walk at the first mtime at or after now minus the store's shortest days/group_days; doomed units are still walked whole. Same sweep at one fixed now, old vs new: identical 232 dry-run lines and summary; 547k -> 54k stats, 58.6 -> 14.8 s wall unthrottled. Ruled out: the lsof/ps open-file pass (one call, only once a unit is doomed). Same day: system-doctor reruns a logstores run whose scan was cut or sweep failed once, LOGS retry_s after it began (logstores_retry), so collector logstores is not blind for a day when du's 600 s budget runs out under the night's load (10-23, 10-29: `~` cut). 10-29 (system-system-20261029T112240Z-5eba): the 1 failed removal of the 10-28 and 10-29 sweeps is the doomed tmp-sandboxes unit $TMPDIR/tmp.QxFTh2pvpF, a killed test_log_stores run's $WORK left with home/cachey/locked at mode 0 (rmtree cannot list it); the only doomed unit of 222 holding a shut directory, no immutable flags. Fixed llm-legs@18b1b341: remove() reopens a shut directory of ours and retries, the suite's trap reopens before rm -rf; the unit is left in place for the next daily sweep to remove. Not fixed: --json drops the per-failure line (say is silenced), so sweeps.jsonl never names a failing path.

rows.title: memlogd job: two ps and a python start per 15 s tick
rows.note: The same cost as cohort:memlogd (its note has the per-tick split and the next lever: one ps a tick, then no python start per tick). Coalition 10-29 07:5x-08:0x over 600 s: 13.0 cpu-s, 2,061 tasks, 5.8 MB (1,878 cpu-s, 297k tasks, 0.8 GB a day); 1.9 GB/day on the 24 h fact is mostly 1 Hz incident ticks (949 on 10-28) and the jump/incident frames (a 200-250 KB ps dump each, frames/ held at 954 MB of its 1 GiB cap) plus chat-load.state.json (95 KB) and chats.json rewritten each tick. 10-29 (system-system-20261029T112240Z-5eba): each ps -axo measures 40-50 ms CPU here (time -p, ~900 processes), not ~110 ms. The job's rise is load: the 1 Hz incident ticks under swap 88 % were 82 on 10-27, 949 on 10-28 and 1,825 by 13:30 on 10-29 against ~5,600 quiet ticks a day, each with a chat-load start and, in the fast phase, a full ps -axo command frame (the frames are the guard's evidence, kept). Ruled out for this cost: date's two forks a tick (tests/test_memlogd.sh fakes date for the day roll, a printf builtin bypasses that seam). One ps a tick saves ~45 ms a tick and needs the test's fake ps rework; the persistent sampler (no python start a tick) remains the larger lever. 10-30 (system-system-20261030T023135Z-005c): 180-253 cpu-s and 31-40k processes an hour at 01:34 and 03:34 against 63 cpu-s and 12k at 02:34: the 1 Hz incident ticks under swap 82-85 % carry the job, as on 10-29; levers unchanged.

rows.title: llm-refresh: ~2,500 processes per 5-min heartbeat
rows.note: Coalition over 600 s (2 heartbeats): 20.0 cpu-s, 5,127 tasks, 6.6 MB. Not run here: a tick probes the real accounts and store (CLAUDE.md cardinal rule), so no per-step split. Reading only: run_tick threads its state through jq per field and per account (`jq ... < <(printf ...)`, ~2-3 tasks each, several per vendor and account) and runs the passive collector (llm-limits) and vendor probes inside the same coalition. Next fixer: time one tick against a CLAUDEB_DIR fixture copy with stub vendor CLIs to split jq plumbing from probes; the plumbing is the output-equivalent lever (one jq per vendor reading the whole state). The heartbeat runs the main checkout's bin/llm-refresh off /Volumes/Work; ~/Library/Logs/llm-refresh.log shows 'Interrupted system call' starts and a mid-edit syntax error, not a cost. 10-29 (system-system-20261029T112240Z-5eba): still not split; tests/test_llm_refresh.sh's collector stub and fixture store are the place to time one tick. Reading: account_rows runs one jq per vendor per caller and next_revive_account two jq per account, so the plumbing is per account times callers. 10-30 (system-system-20261030T023135Z-005c): a fresh fixture tick (tests/test_llm_refresh.sh stubs, 4 vendors x 1 account, PATH shims counting) runs 97 external commands, 89 of them jq: under 5 % of the ~2,250 processes a production heartbeat starts, so the jq plumbing is not the lever. The bulk is the collector llm-limits.sh (2,580 lines, 109 jq sites, sourced per call) and the vendor probes in the same coalition; next fixer: time one passive llm-limits.sh collect against a fixture store. Its 10-28 bash crash reports were limit_hit_bytes, fixed under job-crash:llm-legs/bin/vendor-cli-update.

rows.title: harness-doctor: whole-state rewrite and re-fold every 5 min
rows.note: Coalition over 600 s (2 runs): 18.1 cpu-s, 201 tasks, 7.8 MB. Its own timing (latest.json timing): 13.6 cpu-s, 114 s wall; phases hook_view 32 s, sections 31 s, journals 20 s, transcripts 10 s, judge 10 s, summaries 9 s. Written each run: state.json 5.3 MB whole (files 2.1 MB and seen 1.8 MB of incremental-scan offsets, journal 1.1 MB), hook-runs pickles 4.4 MB, latest.json 1.1 MB, refusal-scan.json 0.8 MB, samples.jsonl 0.7 MB rewritten to trim. Levers for the next fixer: state parts written only when changed (split files/seen out of state.json), samples.jsonl appended and trimmed daily, then profile hook_view and sections. 10-29 (system-system-20261029T112240Z-5eba): samples.jsonl now appended, rewritten about once a day (llm-legs@ae2e03b0, ~195 MB a day). Two consecutive live runs: state.json files changed 27 of 5,407 entries (31 KB of 2.0 MB), seen 55 of 1,197 (42 KB of 1.7 MB), journal 0.94 MB and speed 0.45 MB rewritten whole, hook_map 35 of 132 KB; hook-runs pickles are already appended per run. The next lever is files and seen out of state.json, written only by changed part (~3.6 MB of 5.3 MB a run, ~1 GB a day), but files' dict order feeds c1_expire's events and statusline_fold, so a shard split must keep insertion order or prove it irrelevant; not done here. 10-30 (system-system-20261030T023135Z-005c): unprofiled hook_batches is 1.15 cpu-s a run (983k hook runs, 86.9k batches, re-folded whole every run): the live-list rebuild 0.78 s, setter spans 0.38 s. Skipping the rebuild while the oldest live batch is in span and the setter spans when first is last gave identical batches at 1.05 s (-9 %, ~30 cpu-s a day), not landed. The CPU lever is folding only the runs since the last run's cut and carrying open batches in state. A --json run spawns 68 processes (28 of them git -C in last_fix_at).

rows.title: system-doctor agent: 60 s ticks, harvest and logstores
rows.note: Coalition over 600 s: 7.8 cpu-s, 286 tasks, 5.6 MB (1,124 cpu-s/day). costs in latest.json: a tick 0.39 cpu-s own (ps 0.17, ps_children 0.16: two ps a minute) plus a python start, 1,440 a day; harvest 180 cpu-s/day (4 runs), logstores 128 (its sweep's 34 cpu-s cut by this run's log-sweep fix), dumpstate 7; the judge pass is ~59 s wall a run. The two ps (ps_snapshot 2 s apart) are the tick's measurement, CPU deltas and births between them, not a duplicate. Next lever: read the second snapshot in-process (machine_probe already reads proc_pid_rusage and coalitions by ctypes) instead of a full ps -A args listing, then price the judge pass. 10-29 (system-system-20261029T112240Z-5eba): latest.json costs: a tick 0.275 cpu-s (ps 0.23, ps_children 0.18 cpu-s, their children counted), harvest 167 cpu-s in 4 runs, logstores 265 cpu-s in 2 runs (10-29's retry after the 04:00 sweep timeout). Reading the second snapshot in-process would have to reproduce ps -A -o args for other users' processes and lstart keys, not output-equivalent by construction; not done. 10-30 (system-system-20261030T023135Z-005c): 38-44 cpu-s and ~2,000 processes an hour, unchanged; levers unchanged, not reworked here.

rows.title: tokenmap-scand nightly writes
rows.note: 1.1 GB/day written, 510 cpu-s, 40 processes: the writes are token-map's scan and kinds runs (token-map repository, report-only from this run, no ADD-DIR worktree); 10-29 it was still running at 08:05 after its 05:00 start (13.8 cpu-s per 10 min, no new tasks). The incremental scan's write cut is ssd-writes row token-map/tokenmap/__main__.py (fixed-pending); next fixer: which of scan, rates or kinds writes the GB (the token-map owner). 10-29 (system-system-20261029T112240Z-5eba): the job log's steps, UTC: scan 03:00-09:42 (6.7 h at nice 19 under the night's load; 0.6 h on 10-28), kinds 09:42-11:00, canary and verify to 11:10, html from 11:10. The token-map helper repository had no worktree for this run. 10-30 (system-system-20261030T023135Z-005c): unchanged: token-map repository, no worktree in this run either.

rows.title: worker-run forks per call (machine births, top cause)
rows.note: 10-29 17:47-18:46 1,022 births/s (limit 1,000), worker-run 26 % of the births the ticks saw, then geminib 16 %, (bash) 12 %, claude 9 %: the night's load (worker suites, image legs, bench). causer() charges worker-run with its own forks and every child outside an LLM CLI, so most of its share is the test_worker_run_* suites driving it under fixtures, plus live supervisors, waits and the per-call module sourcing. A traced fixture codex start + supervise + wait --report (BASH_ENV xtrace, one PS4 pid per fork): 313 bash forks and 264 external commands; the spread is flat, no hot loop (the watchdog hop is 30 s and memoized, the wait poll 5 s on a kqueue watcher). Cut, output-equivalent: the script path by parameter expansion (no dirname, basename and their subshells per call), the perl setsid probe on first launch rather than at every source (wait, report, stop launch nothing), codex session_id as grep -m1 into the shell (no head, sed; 7 calls a run), config_value read in-shell, web_search_column and web_search_vendors over the table held in a variable (no cat|awk, 4 calls a start); same trace 577 -> 518 processes; old vs new outputs identical on the session_id, config_value and web-search cases under bash 5 and 3.2, and on 5 invocation forms of the path (relative, absolute, ./, symlink, nested relative symlink). Left, next levers by count: session_transcript's codex find|head (3 a run), session_id's jq .vendor when the caller passes none (4), worker-run-snapshot.sh:330 and :36, worker-model.sh:284. The proof shares blind_spots cohort-proof-work-mix (worker-run's births follow its runs and the suites run against it). 10-30 (system-system-20261030T023135Z-005c): births 15.1 -> 31.7 /s over 7.9 h of night load (suites and live runs) with CPU 0.031 -> 0.003 cores; blind_spots cohort-proof-work-mix holds.

blind_spots.what: the cohort fix proof of llm-legs/bin/statusline.sh
blind_spots.reason: proof() reads tag_rates over tick cpu_top, where a render is claude's reaped CPU, so its baseline reads 0 cores and every statusline fix is refused for no measurable baseline; cohort_sums moves the statusline journal's cpu_ms to the item, proof does not. The journal shows the fixes worked: ~109 ms CPU a render on 10-13, 35-41 ms on 10-17, 10-18 and 10-20, 66 ms on loaded 10-19 (23-135 ms by hour, load-driven).
blind_spots.would_catch_if: tag_rates added statusline_cpu(rows) for the statusline item, as cohort_sums does

blind_spots.what: which short-lived or other users' process writes the internal SSD
blind_spots.reason: Each tick reads the disk counters of this uid's live processes (proc_pid_rusage), but a process that dies between ticks takes its counters along, and other users' counters need root; the 2026-10-04 privileged sample put ~76% of writes on our own short-lived processes. Since 2026-10-13 the root bin/ssd-sampler (owner-consented, installed by `sudo bin/ssd-sampler install`) traces up to 2 min every 3.5 h (cut at 20 s lag, past which fs_usage drops events) and Disk writes lists its shares; between samples the gap stays
blind_spots.would_catch_if: a continuous privileged trace (fs_usage or endpoint security) instead of 10-min samples
blind_spots.unmeasurable: Endpoint Security needs the Apple-granted com.apple.developer.endpoint-security.client entitlement, which no script of ours can hold, and fs_usage drops events past 20 s of lag, which is why the consented root ssd-sampler is cut at 2 min; an unprivileged rule sees only this uid's live processes, so the gap between samples has no meter (2026-10-29)

blind_spots.what: the parents of processes that live less than the 2 s window outside storms
blind_spots.reason: Births are attributed from the newborns still alive at the window's end; a storm (2,000 births/s for 2 min or kernel share 0.5) adds a 60 s census polling every 20 ms, at most every 30 min, so calm hours still lean toward longer-lived children
blind_spots.would_catch_if: an exec event stream (endpoint security, root)
blind_spots.unmeasurable: the only exec event stream on macOS is Endpoint Security, which needs root and the Apple-granted endpoint-security.client entitlement no script of ours can hold; dtrace is blocked under SIP and polling cannot see a process that lives under its interval (2026-10-29)

blind_spots.what: idle wakeups, disk bytes and footprints of items running under another uid (root and _-user Apple daemons, privileged helpers)
blind_spots.reason: proc_pid_rusage of another uid's processes needs root, so those items' cohort score counts CPU and launches only and lists W, D, R and M as unknown; every process of this uid (Chrome, claude, Dia, Figma) is read since 2026-10-13
blind_spots.unmeasurable: proc_pid_rusage of another uid's process fails without root, and the doctors run as Egor's user; a new root sample needs his consent and his sudo install, as bin/ssd-sampler did, so no unprivileged rule can read these terms (2026-10-29)

blind_spots.what: which hs CLI client was inside Hammerspoon when it crashed
blind_spots.reason: A Hammerspoon ipc crash report names no client; an hs killed by a timeout leaves no report of its own, so the client is inferred from the suites running in the tick before
blind_spots.would_catch_if: the hs calls journaled their start, end, exit and caller

blind_spots.what: login items and background helpers macOS registers outside launchd plists (Background Task Management)
blind_spots.reason: Background lists every launchd plist in the agent dirs and every process the ticks saw; the BTM store and `sfltool dumpbtm` need root, so an app's SMAppService helper or login item shows only once it runs
blind_spots.would_catch_if: a consented privileged `sfltool dumpbtm` in the nightly pass
blind_spots.unmeasurable: the Background Task Management store and `sfltool dumpbtm` need root, and the doctors run as Egor's user; a root pass needs his consent and his sudo install, as bin/ssd-sampler did, so no unprivileged rule can list a helper before it runs (2026-10-29)

blind_spots.what: processes a SIGKILLed suite leaves behind, reparented to launchd
blind_spots.reason: Their cause is the nearest live ancestor, launchd, so the tick tags them and the children they reap by their own name (`bash`): a test_slots waiter of night 3131 polled `sleep 0.2` for 13.6 h before a System fixer killed it; nothing names the suite that started it
blind_spots.would_catch_if: suites exported a run tag their children carry (env or process group) and the tick read it

blind_spots.what: the cohort fix proof of a cause whose CPU follows its own work count
blind_spots.reason: proof() compares cores and births/s before and after a fix, not per unit of the cause's work: memlogd's CPU follows its 1 Hz incident ticks (82 on 10-27, 1,825 on 10-29), worker-run's its live runs and hops (a night-only after-window against a 7-day day-and-night baseline), so load reads as a regression and an idle week as a fix.
blind_spots.would_catch_if: proof divided the cause's CPU by its own work count (memlogd ticks by kind from its day log, worker-run runs from the run dirs) or compared the same hours of day before and after

blind_spots.what: the cause of the machine's kernel CPU share (kernel:machine)
blind_spots.reason: The kernel rule names its top cause from the births ranking, yet over 138 ticks of 10-29 16:10-19:06 the kernel share barely followed births (r 0.25; 0.445 at under 400 births/s, 0.488 at 1,200 and more) and followed busy (0.58) and swap-ins (0.36) under swap 97 % full: paging and the compressor, which no births ranking can name. The same hour named worker-run, then geminib, as its cause.
blind_spots.would_catch_if: the kernel rule ranked causes by per-process system time (ri_system_time, values[1] of the rusage struct machine_probe.proc_rusage already reads and drops) beside kernel_task's own CPU, and named paging when the compressor and swap-ins carry the share
